title: Mabel's Sparkleberry Surprise
markdown:
Sunbeams popped over the burrow roof. Mabel the marmot’s whiskers twitched. Today was the Great Berry Jam Contest, and she bounded out kicking dewdrops as if the grass had asked for a drummer. The air smelled of strawberries. Birds, who had opinions, cheered for jam in their own language.

She dashed into her kitchen. Pots gleamed. Jars waited in a row that would have pleased a more anxious cook. Mabel’s prize was Sunshine Swirl, a jam that tasted like a good morning kept in a jar, and it needed one particular ingredient: Sparkleberries. Tiny zippy pink jewels that burst with a fizzy flavour you could not fake with ordinary fruit.

“Where are my Sparkleberries?” The pantry answered with an emptiness that felt personal. Her heart thumped. The contest table would not wait for a marmot to invent a substitute.

A bushy tail appeared in the doorway. Theo the fox, tail already wagging, chirped, “Ready to dazzle?”

Mabel explained the missing jewels. Theo’s ears perked. He tapped his chin as if the chin kept a map. “I saw Gran Ada by the big oak. Basket. Something pink and shiny.”

They hurried to Gran Ada’s cottage. The door was ajar and let out a sweet scent, the sort that makes a contestant both hopeful and slightly jealous. Gran Ada hummed over a pot, stirring as if stirring were a conversation.

“Gran Ada. Sparkleberries. Mine, I think. Or they were this morning.”

Gran Ada blinked, patted her apron, and looked like a person catching up with her own morning. “I was collecting them for a special tea. So pretty. I put them in that blue tin, next to the fluffy things.”

Mabel flew to the high shelf. The blue tin sat where a blue tin should. The fluffy things were not leaves. They were cotton balls, a nest for fruit that liked to roll. She opened the lid. Nestled in the fluff were the Sparkleberries, shimmering like small decisions that had gone right.

“You found them. And kept them safe.”

Theo grinned. “Timing.”

They skipped back. Mabel’s paws flew: berries into the pot, stir, the jam bubbling into a golden swirl with pink pops that announced themselves. She spooned it into jars with the care of someone who had almost arrived at a contest empty-handed.

The contest table groaned under other people’s jars. Rabbits and squirrels stood hopeful. Pipkin Pumble, the judge, a serious badger with a notebook, sniffed each offering as if sniffing were a science.

“Next.”

Mabel, Theo at her elbow, presented Sunshine Swirl. Pipkin tasted. His eyes widened. He scribbled as if the pencil had somewhere to be.

“Tangy. Zesty. And that pop.”

“Sparkleberries,” Mabel said, before she could be modest about it.

Pipkin adjusted his spectacles. “Bold.” He tasted again. A tiny smile arrived and was allowed to stay. “You made it do the work.”

He gave her the Most Inventive Flavor ribbon: bright blue, golden stars, the sort of ribbon that makes a marmot dance whether she means to or not. Theo nudged her paw. Gran Ada, who had come along for the verdict, beamed as if the cotton balls had been part of the recipe all along.

Everyone tasted. Sunshine Swirl, with its fizzy pink punctuation, was the talk of the green. Mabel did not declare the day a marvel of the age. She logged empty pantry / blue tin / cotton nest in her contest book, left a jar for Gran Ada’s tea, and let Theo carry the ribbon as if foxes were the official transport. They dashed off because there were still spoons to wash, and because a winning jam, left alone, will try to tell the whole burrow by itself.
